questionDesk.title: Ask a question. Follow its sources.
questionDesk.intro: Find a passage, then open its source to judge the evidence.
questionDesk.questionPlaceholder: Which decision or rule do you want to understand?

questionDesk.otherOriginals: {count, number} more sources are available in the Sources tab.

questionDesk.zeroLocalBody: The files searched here contain no matching text passage. Word search can miss documents in another language or a format Atlas cannot read; this result does not establish an answer.

questionDesk.limits: Unreadable sources: {unreadable, number} · changed during search: {changed, number} · skipped by read limit: {skipped, number} · matching leads omitted: {omitted, number}. Search matches words and uses the last listed file versions; external edits may appear after a folder refresh.
questionDesk.unknown: No matching passage found in the files read. The answer remains unknown; inspect the unread or omitted files before treating this as absence.
questionDesk.outdated: The folder changed after this search. Search again to use the current files.
questionDesk.wikiCaveat: These are statements on pages, not verified answers. Source freshness does not establish that a claim follows from its source.
questionDesk.noWikiHits: No matching wiki fact or decision in the pages read.
questionDesk.noSourceHits: No matching text in the sources Atlas could read. PDFs and unsupported formats may need another reader.
questionDesk.noCitation: This claim cites no exact place in a source, so it cannot be checked here.

report.agentUnavailable: Connect an agent in the installed app for a draft report. Local evidence remains available below.
report.title: Question report
report.caveat: Read the cited sources before accepting any claim. This draft has not been reviewed or saved to the folder.

fileRefused.shape: Save to wiki needs the four requested report sections, once and in order. This freeform draft remains available for review and export.
fileRefused.no-evidence: Save to wiki needs at least one evidence bullet with its own source citation. The draft remains available for review and export.
fileRefused.citation: Not saved: a citation points at no valid place in a source. Open the source and revise the draft first.
fileRefused.source: Not saved: a cited source is not available in this folder.
fileRefused.unsafe: Not saved: the draft contains an external link, image, or raw HTML. Review it before saving.
fileRefused.changed: Not saved: a cited source changed after the folder was listed. Search again.
fileRefused.anchor: Not saved: a citation does not lead to an exact passage in the current source.

report.printFailed: Could not open the print dialog. The report remains here; try again from the installed app.
report.citationNote: Citations are text addresses from the agent draft. Whether they open reflects the file list at search time; exporting does not re-read the sources.
report.rawFallback: This agent response did not follow the requested four sections. It is shown as written, without inferred headings.
report.readyNotice: Unreviewed question report ready in the main pane. Focus remains where you were working.
report.emptySection: The agent wrote nothing in this section.
report.outdated: This draft refers to an older search or folder version. Search and write the report again before exporting or saving to the wiki.
report.citationUnavailable: This citation does not lead to an exact place in a listed source.
report.externalUnavailable: External links in an agent draft are not opened here.

lede: The project documents you gathered, in whatever format they arrived, and the wiki pages written from them. A source is kept byte for byte, and every claim on a page cites one.

emptyBody: Bring in the documents this project already has: a spec, a slide deck, a spreadsheet, a page you exported. Atlas copies them into sources/ untouched and never opens them until you ask.
stageTitle: The documents you have, as a wiki that cites them

wiki.compileTooltip: The agent reads sources and writes or updates their wiki pages. Saved answers are flagged for separate review.
wiki.lintTooltip: The agent reads the wiki pages and reports disagreements, superseded claims, missing links and names without a page. It writes nothing.
wiki.proposeTooltip: The agent reads these pages and proposes one ontology concept. The write waits for your permission.
wiki.empty: No wiki pages yet. A page is Markdown with no kind:, in the shape wiki/_template.md holds.
wiki.offTemplateCount: {count, plural, one {# page does not fit the template} other {# pages do not fit the template}}
wiki.transfer: The coding agent sends requests directly to its provider; Atlas does not record that traffic. Wiki pages that fit the template can be saved automatically. Saved answers always need separate review.
wiki.compileWebLimit: Writing wiki pages needs a coding agent running on this computer, which only the app can start. Reading and editing pages works here.
wiki.agentMissing: Connect a coding agent to check the wiki and write wiki pages from sources.
wiki.offTemplateReason: Does not fit the wiki template: {code}. Open the page to see what to change.
wiki.offTemplateAriaLabel: How this page differs from the wiki template
wiki.offTemplateBody: Fix what follows and it reads the same way every other page does.
wiki.originalMissing: Cites {name}, which is not in this folder.
wiki.emptyNoTemplate: No wiki pages yet, and no template in this folder. Start a wiki from Settings › Ontology folder: it writes wiki/_template.md, the shape every page follows.
wiki.candidatesMore: {count, plural, one {# more name} other {# more names}}
wiki.candidatesTooltip: Names the last check saw on three or more pages with no page of their own. Only what the code builds, a domain, a capability or an element, can be proposed as a concept on the map; people and organisations stay names in the wiki.
wiki.fileAnswerTooltip: Write the last answer as a wiki page under wiki/answers/, with the files it cited as its sources. It is checked against the same page format as every page.
wiki.fileAnswerRejected: Not saved: the answer does not match the page format ({code}). Ask for citations and try again.
wiki.fixTooltip: The agent fixes this on the pages named: both values with both citations for a disagreement, the current value first for a superseded claim, links both ways for a missing link.
wiki.newPageTooltip: Start a page you write yourself: the template's sections and created_by: human, empty until you fill it in any editor. The list updates by itself.
wiki.newPageDialogBody: Create a Markdown draft with the standard structure ready to fill in.
wiki.newPagePreviewExample: Example path until you enter a title
wiki.newPageFailed: Could not make the page. Check the folder can be written.
wiki.askNextDone: From the next page on, each write asks for permission. Change it back in Settings › Ontology folder.
wiki.undoFailed: Could not undo: the file is already gone or the folder is not writable.
wiki.linkFindingsAriaLabel: How this page connects inside the folder
wiki.linkFindingsBody: The page fits the template. What follows is about the folder: things no single page can see about itself.
wiki.fixWithAgentTooltip: The agent brings this page back to the template. A fixed page that fits is saved as it is; one that does not asks for your permission first.
wiki.fixWithAgentTooltipAsk: The agent brings this page back to the template. Each write asks for your permission.
wiki.fixMyselfTooltip: Selects this page's file in Finder. Edit it in any editor; the list updates.
wiki.technical: Technical detail · check codes and line numbers
wiki.technicalNote: The wiki-validate command and the validate_wiki tool report these same codes.

where.unknown: a line with no recorded number

kind-present.what: This page carries the marker (kind) that puts a document on the map, and a wiki page does not belong on the map.
kind-present.do: Delete that line, or move the file out of the wiki folder if it really is a concept.

missing-field.what: The info block at the top of the file has no {field} line.

section-order-missing.what: The page needs all five sections and {missing} is not there.
section-order-missing.do: Add the missing section, heading alone if you like. "Nothing here" is itself something a reader learns.

section-order-sequence.what: The sections are in a different order: right now it reads {found}.

uncited-fact.what: No source backs up what is written at {where}.
uncited-fact.do: Point it at one place in one source, or move it into the Not in sources section at the end of the page if you cannot.

bad-citation.what: A citation at {where} cannot be read.
bad-citation.do: Make it name the source file and the place inside it. The exact shape is under the technical detail.

bad-truncation-record-shape.what: The line that records how far a source was read (sources_truncated) is not a list of paths.
bad-truncation-record-shape.do: Write the path of each source that was read only in part, as a list.

bad-truncation-record-path.what: {path} is recorded as read only in part, but it is not among the sources this page uses.
bad-truncation-record-path.do: Add it to the list of sources, or remove that line.

citation-target-missing-folder.what: {path} is cited but that file is not in this folder.
citation-target-missing-folder.do: A citation a reader cannot open is not a citation: put the file in this folder, or fix the citation.

citation-target-missing-sources.what: {path} is cited but it is not among the sources this page uses.
citation-target-missing-sources.do: Add it to the list of sources, or fix the citation.

describes-needs-approval.what: This page says it speaks for a concept (describes), and that is a claim about the map a person has to confirm.
describes-needs-approval.do: Read it and set the status to reviewed, or remove that line.

dangling-wikilink.what: The link at {where} points at {target}, and there is no such page in this folder.
dangling-wikilink.do: Link to a page that exists, or write that page.

orphan-page.what: No other page points at this one yet.
orphan-page.do: Link it from the page that talks about its topic and it becomes easy to find.

shared-source-unlinked.what: {other} is written from the same source ({sources}), and neither page points at the other.
shared-source-unlinked.do: Link one of them to the other.

graph.title: Graph
graph.counts: {sources, plural, one {# source} other {# sources}} · {pages, plural, one {# page} other {# pages}} · {concepts, plural, one {# concept} other {# concepts}} · {cites, number} cites · {mentions, number} mentions
graph.countsIsland: {sources, plural, one {# source} other {# sources}} · {pages, plural, one {# page} other {# pages}} · {cites, number} cites
graph.empty: Nothing to show yet. Once Write wiki page writes a page, this shows which source it came from and which concepts it names.
graph.canvasAria: The library graph: raw sources, wiki pages, and the concepts those pages name.
graph.legend: Sources stand on the left, the pages written from them beside, and the concepts those pages name on the right; the lines run from a source to the page that read it. A filled circle is a page, a square a source, a ring a concept on the map. A thicker line is a citation, a dashed one a mention. Scroll to zoom, drag the background to move, press a dot for a card beside it.
graph.legendShort: A circle is a wiki page, a square a source, a ring a concept.
graph.legendCardOpen: A filled circle is a page, a square a source, a ring a concept on the map. A thicker line is a citation, a dashed one a mention, either way. Press Escape, or the same dot again, to close the card.
graph.legendShortCardOpen: A circle is a page, a square a source, a ring a concept. Escape closes the card.
graph.legendIslands: Past a few hundred files the picture is a map of islands: each island is one concept and the pages that name it, with the files those pages were written from packed around them. Unsorted holds pages naming no concept; Unread is the band under the islands: files no page has read yet. An amber dot is a page whose files changed since it was written. Scroll to zoom in until names appear; press a dot for a card beside it.
graph.describeIsland: {name}: an island of {pages, number} pages and the {sources, number} files they read. Press it to open them as columns; zoom in for their names.
graph.announceIsland: Island {name}, {position, number} of {total, number}: {pages, number} pages and {sources, number} files. Enter opens it as columns.
graph.describeUnread: Unread: {sources, number} files no page has read yet. Press it for where to start.
graph.unreadPressed: {sources, number} files no page has read yet, so there is nothing between them to draw. Each is marked no wiki page in the Sources list; Write wiki page, above the picture, starts on the first.
graph.keys: Arrow keys move between dots, Enter opens a card beside the one you are on, Escape closes it.
graph.fitDone: The whole picture is already framed

describe.source: {name}: a source file. A thick line leads to the page written from it; no line means it has no wiki page yet. Press for a card beside it.
describe.page: {name}: a wiki page. Thick lines lead to the sources it cites, dashed lines to concepts it names. Press for a card beside it.
describe.concept: {name}: a concept on the map. The dashed lines lead to the wiki pages it names or was drawn from. Press for a card beside it.

describeOpen.source: {name}: a source file. A thick line leads to the page written from it; no line means it has no wiki page yet. Its card is open beside it: Escape, or press again, closes it.
describeOpen.page: {name}: a wiki page. Thick lines lead to the sources it cites, dashed lines to concepts it names. Its card is open beside it: Escape, or press again, closes it.
describeOpen.concept: {name}: a concept on the map. The dashed lines lead to the wiki pages it names or was drawn from. Its card is open beside it: Escape, or press again, closes it.

undoneReason.notDraft: It did not read status: draft, and a schedule writes drafts only.
undoneReason.duplicateKey: The info block at the top of the page had two {key}: lines, so readers could disagree about it.
undoneReason.forbiddenKey: It carried a {key}: line, which only a person may add.
undoneReason.noFrontmatter: It had no info block at the top, so it could not be read as a draft.
undoneReason.unreadable: Atlas could not read it back to check it.

ledger.undoneCopy: The text Atlas took out is saved in {copy}.
ledger.leftAsIs: {page} changed after this run wrote it; Atlas left it as is.

sheet.redraftHint: The agent runs once for the changed sources only; the new page waits as a draft.
sheet.markHint: The row in Sources turns amber. Nothing is written.
sheet.noAgent: No coding agent is ready on this Mac, so a service check cannot run yet. A source consistency check can.
